findings.claim: The new latchedBoardH reset is keyed on a moveCount TRANSITION to 0, but latchedBoardH is written independently of moveCount - so any deal-to-deal hop with no move in between (demo Stop before Start, Daily Play then immediate New game) never resets it and the fresh deal inherits the previous deal's chrome-shrunk height for its entire life.
findings.note: VERIFIED FIXED. dealGeneration is bumped at Game.swift:181, inside deal(), which I confirmed is the ONLY fresh-board path reachable from the UI: grep for `tableau = ` / `moveCount = 0` in Game.swift yields exactly deal() (169-180), restore() (271) and undo() (425). restore() is called only from init() (Game.swift:146), before any view exists and while latchedBoardH is already its 0 default, so it correctly needs no bump. newRandomGame/restartDeal/playChallenge/showSolution/the deal alert all funnel through deal(). The bump sits before persist() and after stopDemo(), which is right: showSolution re-arms demoing AFTER deal() returns, so the view sees one coalesced update carrying both dealGeneration+1 and the final chrome state. Observer-ordering race checked and benign: whichever of .onChange(of: game.dealGeneration) and .onChange(of: liveH) runs first, the end state is either the new liveH (correct) or 0 (i.e. unlatched, which then latches on the next liveH measurement exactly as a fresh deal does). @Published private(set) is consistent with how ContentView reads it (plain read through @StateObject; only Game mutates). &+= wraparound is harmless since onChange only tests inequality. xcodebuild BUILD SUCCEEDED on iPhone 16 Pro / iOS 18.5, clean derived data.

findings.claim: latchedBoardH is scoped per-deal but is a function of the container size, and nothing invalidated it when the container size changed; a portrait->landscape->portrait round trip (or a rotation intermediate near-square frame classified as portrait) could pin the board at a wrong height for the rest of the deal.
findings.note: VERIFIED FIXED, and the two claims I was asked to attack both hold. (a) ATTACHMENT: .onChange(of: geo.size) at ContentView.swift:182 is a modifier on the ZStack at :100, which is the unconditional content of the ROOT GeometryReader { geo } at :66 - not the inner board-area reader at :132. The ZStack is always in the hierarchy (both orientation branches live inside it), so the closure re-runs on every geo.size delivery and the iOS 17 two-parameter onChange stores/compares the previous CGSize; deployment target is 17.0 (project.pbxproj:142,170) so the form is legal, and the build compiles. Any rotation intermediate SwiftUI chooses to deliver therefore invalidates the latch, and the FINAL size delivery invalidates whatever the intermediates latched. (b) NO PULSE REINTRODUCED: geo.size is the root reader's proposal (screen minus safe area). A GeometryReader unconditionally accepts its proposal and its content cannot feed back into its size, so the chrome the latch guards against (toolbar FlowLayout gaining the Finish pill row at :238ff, demo headline rewrap at :552-555) is strictly INSIDE the ZStack and provably cannot move geo.size. The reset therefore cannot fire on chrome wobble. (c) The reset does not leave a lasting unlatched window: on rotation back into portrait the branch at :132 is re-created and .onChange(of: liveH, initial: true) at :158 immediately re-latches at the current height; on an in-place safe-area/keyboard change liveH changes with geo.size, so the very next pass re-latches. shrinkLatchCount correctly not reset here (card count, size-independent).

findings.claim: The iOS G, T and X token bodies were matched by nothing constraining their field indices or destinations, and the web copy pinned only F/G/C, so a one-sided drift in three of the five tokens shipped with CI green.
findings.note: VERIFIED FIXED BY MUTATION on the web half (the iOS half was mutation-verified in round 1 and Model/Game.swift's applyDemoToken is untouched by this commit). Baseline npm test 68/68. I rsync'd to a scratch tree and ran six independent index.html mutations, each confirmed to have actually landed via diff: T destination t[d]->t[s]; T src/dst fields swapped (col(1)/col(3) -> col(3)/col(1)); T run index +f[2]->+f[1]; X destination t[d]->t[0]; X cell index +f[1]->+f[2]; X guard ||d<0 deleted. All six produced 67 pass / 1 fail, and in every case the single failure was exactly 'web applyDemoToken shares the iOS/solver token format'. All five tokens are now pinned as contiguous normalised bodies on both sides.

findings.claim: The whole-board card width is a live function of bg.size.height, and that height is NOT latched: the toolbar's FlowLayout row count and the demo bar's wrapping headline both change mid-deal in BOTH directions, so once the shrink is engaged the entire board rescales up and down again inside the caller's withAnimation.
findings.note: Still fixed. boardH = min(liveH, latch) at :134 is unchanged; this round only touched the latch's INVALIDATION, and both invalidation channels (dealGeneration, geo.size) fire on events that are not chrome wobble, so the monotone-within-a-deal contract that closed this finding is intact. Residual (inherent, documented at :175-181, not a defect): after a container-size change the latch is cleared and re-seeded at the first subsequent measurement, so the board is sized live for that instant - but :158's initial:true and the fact that liveH always moves with geo.size mean the re-seed happens on the same or next pass.
